Usage

Inertia tensor of the point cloud (3,3) (from the central second moment, assuming equal mass and a total mass of 1).

I_xx = mean(y²+z²), I_yy = mean(x²+z²), I_zz = mean(x²+y²), I_xy = -mean(xy), I_xz = -mean(xz), I_yz = -mean(yz). With the covariance C this is equivalent to I = tr(C)·E₃ − C (E₃ is the identity matrix). Symmetric, positive semi-definite. Translation-invariant because of centroid centring.

Returns

np.ndarray, shape (3, 3)

Symmetric inertia tensor.

Supplement:

• Units are length² (points are treated as equal masses of mass 1, so density does not enter). Rotating the point cloud maps it to R I Rᵀ; the eigenvalues (principal_moments) are rotation invariants and the eigenvectors are the principal axes (moment_axes).

• The input is (N,3) with N >= 1 (1 point gives the zero matrix). Invalid shape or non-finite values raise ValueError.

• Relation to the covariance C: I = tr(C)·E₃ - C; C and I have the same eigenvectors, and the eigenvalues are tr(C) - c_i.

• These are moments of the sample points, not of the solid (volume), so the same shape gives different values with uneven point density. To even out density, apply voxel_grid_downsample beforehand. Deterministic.

The 3d op inertia_tensor bridged into the 2-D evolution registry. The implementation is the same; only the calling convention is adapted to op(v, a, b). This op has no tuning points; neither a nor b is used.
